scope: Long-term ambition: complete human ectogenesis from IVF through birth. This first release maps distinct developmental research stages and tests abstract software fixtures. It does not establish a wall-powered gestation machine, surrogacy replacement or reduced congenital defects.

stages.label: Preimplantation development
stages.boundary: A separate stage; this ledger does not provide a continuous human gestation pathway.

stages.label: Implantation and placental interface formation
stages.boundary: Morphogenesis or an interface model is not a functional placenta sustaining complete gestation.

stages.label: Postimplantation embryonic development
stages.boundary: Intervals remain in the source species' notation; no conversion into human gestational equivalence.

stages.label: Partial support of an already-developed fetus
stages.boundary: Support starts after prior development in utero; it cannot establish IVF-to-birth gestation.

stages.label: Transition from support to neonatal life
stages.boundary: Short-term transition and survival are separate from long-term developmental outcomes.

stages.label: Developmental and longer-term outcomes
stages.boundary: Survival or physiological stability cannot substitute for controlled developmental and long-term follow-up endpoints.

stages.label: Continuous IVF-to-birth gestation
stages.boundary: An explicitly undemonstrated human ambition in this bounded ledger; separate reports cannot be concatenated into proof.

sources.title: Partridge et al., extra-uterine support of premature lambs (2017)
sources.interval: Already-developed fetal lambs; support up to 28 days
sources.boundary: Preclinical partial gestation support; not IVF-to-birth and not a demonstrated human treatment.

sources.title: Aguilera-Castrejon et al., ex utero mouse embryogenesis (2021)
sources.interval: Approximately E5.5–E11; up to six days
sources.boundary: Mouse embryos begin after implantation; no birth or complete human gestation demonstrated.

sources.title: Usuda et al., developmental limitations during artificial placenta support (2023)
sources.interval: Six fetuses starting at 93–94 gestational days in Methods (abstract reports 95 days); support up to 336 hours (14 days)
sources.boundary: Physiological support coexisted with reduced somatic and organ growth versus in-utero controls; stability is not normal development.

sources.title: FDA background presentation on artificial womb technology (2023)
sources.interval: Intended bridge from extreme preterm birth to later gestation; not a trial interval
sources.boundary: Regulatory discussion of intended use and evaluation; not authorization, a trial result, complete gestation, or clinical efficacy.

sources.title: Hospital Clinic BCNatal fetaLife announcement (2026-07-03)
sources.interval: Announced support up to 21 days; proposed first-in-human study in 2028–2029, conditional on investment
sources.boundary: Institutional announcement, with proposed future human study rather than human results; not IVF-to-birth evidence.

claims.text: The 2017 report describes partial extra-uterine support of fetal lambs for up to 28 days.
claims.interval: Already-developed fetal lambs; up to 28 days
claims.boundary: The interval starts after development in a uterus and does not demonstrate complete ectogenesis.

claims.text: The 2021 report describes mouse postimplantation development across an approximately E5.5–E11 interval.
claims.interval: Approximately E5.5–E11; up to six days
claims.boundary: The embryos did not develop through birth; this interval is not converted into a human interval.

claims.text: The 2023 ovine report found reduced somatic and organ growth during support relative to in-utero controls.
claims.interval: 93–94-day starting fetuses in Methods (abstract reports 95 days); up to 14 days of support
claims.boundary: Physiological support cannot be taken as proof of normal development or later human benefit.

claims.text: FDA's 2023 discussion frames artificial womb technology as a possible bridge for extremely premature infants.
claims.interval: Proposed clinical support interval, not measured in a trial
claims.boundary: Intended use and discussion of study design do not establish a treatment result.

claims.text: BCNatal announced 21-day support in an ovine model, neonatal transition, and follow-up of one sheep; it proposed a future human study.
claims.interval: Up to 21 days announced; proposed human study in 2028–2029
claims.boundary: Announcement-level evidence and prospective timeline; no human result or complete gestation demonstrated.

claims.text: A continuous artificial system supporting a human from IVF through birth remains an undemonstrated ambition in this ledger.
claims.interval: Complete IVF-to-birth interval; no demonstrated interval in this ledger
claims.boundary: A bounded ledger is not a systematic review or a claim that this ambition is impossible.

claims.text: Replacing gestational surrogacy is a proposed future application without demonstrated support in this ledger.
claims.interval: Complete human gestation and subsequent outcomes required
claims.boundary: Partial fetal support cannot establish replacement of an entire pregnancy.

claims.text: Reduced congenital-defect incidence is an unassessed proposed benefit in this ledger.
claims.interval: Comparative developmental and longer-term outcome evidence required
claims.boundary: Environmental control or absence of pregnancy does not itself imply fewer congenital defects.

requirements.text: Demonstrate continuous support across all human developmental stages with compatible interfaces and independently assessed outcomes.
Assess developmental function, growth and adverse outcomes separately from physiological support and survival.
Preserve species and actual developmental intervals when comparing embryo and fetal-support evidence.
Establish any proposed human reproductive or congenital-defect benefit using appropriate comparative evidence.
